author: BowlOfRed
text:
Can you see if your kernel does in fact support the syscall?  I think the following should test that.  If you get errno 38, that would suggest the call is not in your kernel.
import ctypes, os
libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
fd = libc.syscall(434, os.getpid(), 0)
if fd >= 0:
    print(f"Success, fd:{fd}")
else:
    print(f"Unsupported, errno: {ctypes.get_errno()}")

author: MartinBonner
text: Problem solved.  I am running Ubuntu 24.04, but some of our customers are running much older distros than that.  sys/fd.h in the container used to build python doesn’t have pidfd_open defined, so Python skips it.
